dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:5901.text: The surrounding buildings below a hall. Formed from 广, with 無 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5902.text: A covered gallery, 廡. Formed from 广, with 虜 indicating the sound. Read like 鹵.

shuowen:5903.text: A kitchen. Formed from 广, with 包 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5904.text: A kitchen building. Formed from 广, with 尌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5905.text: A store for war chariots. Formed from 車 beneath 广.

shuowen:5906.text: A horse stable. Formed from 广, with 㲃 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Two hundred fourteen horses make a stable, and each stable has a groom.”

shuowen:5907.text: The east and west walls. Formed from 广, with 予 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5908.text: A wall. Formed from 广, with 辟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5909.text: The great building of a palace hall. Formed from 广, with 黃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5910.text: A store for fodder and straw. Formed from 广, with 會 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5911.text: A granary by a water trough or channel; the phrase 水槽倉 is uncertain. Formed from 广, with 臾 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a granary without a roof.

shuowen:5912.text: To screen or cover. Formed from 广, with 幷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5913.text: A privy, 清. Formed from 广, with 則 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5914.text: One and a half mu, the dwelling-place of one household. Formed from 广, 里, 八 and 土.

shuowen:5915.text: Beneath a roof’s concave tiles. Another explanation: retaining ropes. Formed from 广, with abbreviated 𨳮 indicating the sound. Read like 環.

shuowen:5916.text: The meeting place among a building’s steps. Formed from 广, with 怱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5917.text: Broad. Formed from 广, with 侈 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Discourses of the States says: “Along the ditch, broaden our ground.”

shuowen:5918.text: An edge or side. Formed from 广, with 兼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5919.text: An open, spreading building. Formed from 广, with 秅 indicating the sound. Jiyin has a county called 㢉.

shuowen:5920.text: A high building. Formed from 广, with 龍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5921.text: A mountain dwelling. Another explanation: below. Formed from 广, with 氐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5922.text: To obstruct and stop. Formed from 广, with 至 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5923.text: To settle peacefully. Formed from 广, with 嬰 indicating the sound. Julu has Yingtao County, 廮陶.

shuowen:5924.text: To lodge. Formed from 广, with 犮 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Where the Earl of Shao lodged.”

shuowen:5925.text: A dwelling sunken in the middle. Formed from 广, with 卑 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a low building. Some read it like 逋.

shuowen:5926.text: Shade or shelter. Formed from 广, with 比 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5927.text: A multitude beneath a roof. Formed from 广 and 炗; 炗 is ancient-script 光.

shuowen:5928.text: To store and place beneath a roof. Formed from 广, with 寺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5929.text: A portable dwelling. Formed from 广, with 異 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5930.text: A building’s open latticework, 麗廔. Formed from 广, with 婁 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to plant, 穜; this alternative is uncertain.

shuowen:5931.text: A building leaning downward from above. Formed from 广, with 隹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5932.text: A building collapsing. Formed from 广, with 發 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5933.text: Rotten wood in an old building. Formed from 广, with 酉 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “If an ox lows at night, it is 𢉷,” smelling like rotten wood.

shuowen:5934.text: A small, poor dwelling. Formed from 广, with 堇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5935.text: The manner of honoring ancestors. Formed from 广, with 朝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5936.text: People relying on one another. Formed from 广, with 且 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5937.text: A cramped building. Formed from 广, with 曷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5938.text: To open up or set a building back, 郤屋; the precise gloss is uncertain. Formed from 广, with 屰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5939.text: To display carriages and garments in the courtyard. Formed from 广, with 欽 indicating the sound. Read like 歆.

shuowen:5940.text: Empty. Formed from 广, with 膠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5941.text: A building. Formed from 广, with 夏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5942.text: The east and west side galleries. Formed from 广, with 郎 indicating the sound. The Book of Han also uses 郎.

shuowen:5943.text: A gallery. Formed from 广, with 相 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5944.text: Sacrificing to mountains is called 庪縣. Formed from 广, with 技 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5945.text: A place name. Formed from 广; further details are unknown.

shuowen:5946.text: A surname. Formed from 广; further details are unknown. It should simply be an abbreviated 廫.

shuowen:5947.text: A rocky mountain cliff where people can dwell. Pictographic. All characters in this group are formed from 厂.

shuowen:5948.text: A mountain’s edge. Formed from 厂, with 圭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5949.text: 厜㕒, a mountain summit. Formed from 厂, with 垂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5950.text: The summit 厜㕒. Formed from 厂, with 義 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5951.text: Lofty, 崟. Another explanation: a place name. Formed from 厂, with 敢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5952.text: A spring issuing sideways. Formed from 厂, with 晷 indicating the sound. Read like 軌.

shuowen:5953.text: To smooth stone. Formed from 厂, with 氐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5954.text: To set a stone in motion. Formed from 厂, with 欮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5955.text: A dry stone, 旱石; the recorded gloss is uncertain. Formed from 厂, with abbreviated 蠆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5956.text: 厱諸, a stone used to work jade. Formed from 厂, with 僉 indicating the sound. Read like 藍.

shuowen:5957.text: To put in order. Formed from 厂, with 秝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5958.text: A stone’s sharpness. Formed from 厂, with 異 indicating the sound. Read like 枲.

shuowen:5959.text: A beautiful stone. Formed from 厂, with 古 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5960.text: 唐厗, a stone. Formed from 厂, with abbreviated 屖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5961.text: The sound of stones. Formed from 厂, with 立 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5962.text: Poor stony ground. Formed from 厂, with 兒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5963.text: Stony ground. Formed from 厂, with 金 indicating the sound. Read like 紟.

shuowen:5964.text: Visible between stones. Formed from 厂, with 甫 indicating the sound. Read like 敷.

shuowen:5965.text: A whetstone. Formed from 厂, with 㫺 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Stones from other mountains can serve as whetstones.”

shuowen:5966.text: A large stone. Formed from 厂, with 尨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5967.text: Appearing above a bank. Formed from 厂 and abbreviated 之. Read like 躍.

shuowen:5968.text: Inclined, 𠪮. Formed from 厂, with 夾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5969.text: To incline sideways. Formed from 人 beneath 厂.

shuowen:5970.text: Inclined. Formed from 厂, with 辟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5971.text: Hidden. Formed from 厂, with 非 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5972.text: To press down. Formed from 厂, with 猒 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to join.

shuowen:5973.text: To look upward. Formed from 人 above 厂. Another explanation: an eave timber, called 桷 in Qin and 厃 in Qi.

shuowen:5974.text: A round thing that tilts and rolls. Formed from reversed 仄. All characters in this group are formed from 丸.

shuowen:5975.text: After eating, a bird of prey spits out skin and hair in a pellet. Formed from 丸, with 咼 indicating the sound. Read like 骫.

shuowen:5976.text: The cooking or ripening of a ball-shaped thing. Formed from 丸, with 而 indicating the sound; the gloss 丸之孰 is uncertain.

shuowen:5978.text: Being high up and afraid. Formed from 厃, stopping oneself with 卪. All characters in this group are formed from 危.

shuowen:5979.text: Uneven or precipitous, 㩻䧢. Formed from 危, with 支 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5980.text: Mountain stone. Beneath 厂, 囗 depicts its form. All characters in this group are formed from 石.

shuowen:5981.text: The raw ore of copper and iron. Formed from 石, with 黃 indicating the sound. Read like 穬.

shuowen:5982.text: Patterned stone. Formed from 石, with 昜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5983.text: Stone next in quality to jade. Formed from 石, with 耎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5984.text: Stone usable for arrowheads. Formed from 石, with 奴 indicating the sound. The Book of Xia says: “Liangzhou offers stone arrowheads and cinnabar.” The Spring and Autumn Discourses of the States says: “The Sushen offered 楛 arrows with stone heads.”

shuowen:5985.text: A poisonous stone from Hanzhong. Formed from 石, with 與 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5986.text: A stone standing alone. Donghai has Mount Jieshi. Formed from 石, with 曷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5987.text: A whetstone. Another explanation: red in color. Formed from 石, with 兼 indicating the sound. Read like 鎌.

shuowen:5988.text: A whetstone. Formed from 石, with 叚 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Gongsun Xia of Zheng had the courtesy name Zishi.”

shuowen:5989.text: Small stones. Formed from 石, with 樂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5990.text: Waterside stones. Formed from 石, with 巩 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Que Gong’s armor.”

shuowen:5991.text: A river islet having stones. Formed from 石, with 責 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5992.text: An upright stone. Formed from 石, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5993.text: Steep or high, 陖. Formed from 石, with 㒸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5994.text: To fall. Formed from 石, with 員 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Five stones fell in Song.”

shuowen:5995.text: The sound of broken stones falling. Formed from 石, with 炙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5996.text: The sound of stones. Formed from 石, with 告 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5997.text: The sound of stones. Formed from 石, with 良 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5998.text: The sound of stones. Formed from 石, with abbreviated 學 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5999.text: Hard stone. Formed from 石, with 吉 indicating the sound. Another explanation: jutting out.

shuowen:6000.text: The sound of stones. Formed from 石, with 盍 indicating the sound.
